## Error and Power(24-points)

A veterinarian wants to investigate whether Labrador Retrievers and Golden Retrievers differ in their average daily exercise time. The veterinarian randomly samples 100 dogs from each breed and records the number of minutes each dog exercises per day. The hypothesis test was set up as follows: 

$Ho: \mu_g - \mu_l = 0$

$Ha: \mu_g - \mu_l \neq 0$

Prior to the study, previous research suggests that the effect size for the true difference in means was equal to 5-minutes. At n = 200 (100 each), they conducted a power analysis and calculated power to be .74. This hypothesis test uses $\alpha$ = 0.05. 

Please use this context to answer the following questions. 

1. In words and in the context of the problem, interpret the value .74.

\vspace{20 mm}

2. Calculate the probability of making a Type-II error, and calculate the probability of making a Type-I error. 

\vspace{20 mm}

a. We could have only made a Type-II error, and not a Type-I error.

7. Below is our null distribution, with an alternative distribution (effect size) centered at 7. Shade in the area that would represent the probability of rejecting the null hypothesis correctly. Note: the gray area on the plot represents the rejection region.
```{r}
#| echo: false 
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(ggplot2)

library(ggplot2)

SE <- 1.852
alpha <- 0.05
effect_size <- 7

crit <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * SE

x <- seq(-6, 12, length.out = 1000)

df <- data.frame(
  x = rep(x, 2),
  density = c(
    dnorm(x, mean = 0, sd = SE),
    dnorm(x, mean = effect_size, sd = SE)
  ),
  distribution = factor(
    rep(c("Null", "Alternative"), each = length(x)),
    levels = c("Null", "Alternative")
  )
)

ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = density, linetype = distribution)) +
  geom_area(
    data = subset(df, distribution == "Null" & x <= -crit),
    aes(x = x, y = density),
    fill = "gray75",
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_area(
    data = subset(df, distribution == "Null" & x >= crit),
    aes(x = x, y = density),
    fill = "gray75",
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = c(-crit, crit),
    linetype = "dotted"
  ) +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c("Null" = "solid", "Alternative" = "dashed")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(-5, 0, 5, 7, 10)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Difference in Sample Means (minutes)",
    y = "Density",
    linetype = "Distribution"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

7. See the following graph to answer the next question. 

```{r}
#| echo: false

# Load the ggplot2 library for plotting
library(ggplot2)

# Set the individual test significance level (alpha)
alpha <- 0.05

# Define the range of comparisons (m) from 1 to 10
m_values <- 1:10

# Calculate the Familywise Error Rate (FWER) for each m
# FWER = 1 - (1 - alpha)^m
fwer_values <- 1 - (1 - alpha)^m_values

# Create a data frame for plotting
plot_data <- data.frame(
  m = m_values,
  FWER = fwer_values
)

# Plot the FWER vs. the number of comparisons (m)
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = m, y = FWER)) +
  
  # Add the line and points for the FWER
  geom_line(color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "darkblue", size = 3) +
  
  # Add a horizontal line at the nominal alpha level (0.05)
  geom_hline(yintercept = alpha, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  
  # Add labels and title
  labs(
    title = expression(paste("Inflation of Familywise Error Rate (FWER) as m Increases")),
    subtitle = "alpha = 0.05",
    x = "Number of Comparisons (m)",
    y = "Familywise Error Rate (FWER)"
  ) +
  
  # Customize scales
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = m_values) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, max(fwer_values) + 0.05, 0.05)) +
  
  # Apply a clean theme
  theme_minimal()
```

4. Below is output from the chi-square test and the chi-square distribution your test statistic follows. On the chi-square graph, draw how the p-value for this test was calculated. Next, fill in the title of your plot with the correct number of degrees of freedom.

$\chi^2$ = 138

$p-value$ = < 0.001

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)

data(HairEyeColor)

# Combine across gender
hair_eye <- margin.table(HairEyeColor, c(1, 2))

# Chi-square test of independence
test <- chisq.test(hair_eye)

# Test statistic and degrees of freedom
chi_stat <- as.numeric(test$statistic)
df <- as.numeric(test$parameter)

# Create chi-square distribution
x <- seq(0, 200, length.out = 1000)

chi_data <- tibble(
  x = x,
  density = dchisq(x, df = df)
)

# Plot
ggplot(chi_data, aes(x = x, y = density)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 200, by = 20),
    limits = c(0, 200)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Chi-square distribution with _________ degrees of freedom",
    x = "",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

#### Formula sheet 

$df$ = n - 1

$df$ = $min(n_1 - 1, n_2 - 1)$

$df$ = (r-1) * (c-1)

$df$ = k-1 

$df_{\text{numerator}}$ = k-1 

$df_{\text{denominator}}$ = N-k

$\chi^2 = \sum \frac{(O - E)^2}{E}$

$F = \frac{MS_{\text{between}}}{MS_{\text{within}}}$

$F = \frac{SS_{\text{between}}/(k-1)}{SS_{\text{within}}/(n-k)}$

$\text{SS}_{\text{Between}} = \sum_{i=1}^{k} n_i (\bar{X}_i - \bar{X}_{\text{grand}})^2$

$\text{SS}_{\text{Within}} = \sum_{i=1}^{k} \sum_{j=1}^{n_i} (X_{ij} - \bar{X}_i)^2$

$E_{ij} = \frac{(\text{row total}_i)(\text{column total}_j)}{\text{grand total}}$

$E_i = n p_i$

where n is the total sample size and $p_i$ is the hypothesized probability in category i.

all pairwise comparisons: $\frac{k(k-1)}{2}$
